name: legitimate-brand-tld
description:
False-positive resistance for a sender on a brand's own top-level domain. A name under `.apple` can only be Apple's (ICANN's Specification 13 restricts registrations in a brand TLD to the operator, its affiliates and its trademark licensees), so an authenticated notice with a display name saying Apple, sent from Apple's own TLD, must not be reported as impersonation, as it would be if a claim were checked only against the brand table's listed `.com` domains. The impersonation rule must still recognise the claim; the point is that the claim is satisfied, not that the name stops making one.

The security-advice link carries the second half, in the shape of a genuine card issuer's notice: a footer showing the brand's `.com` domain and linking to a short name under the brand's own TLD. Read as a brand's address leading somewhere that is not the brand, it would be a `critical` displayed/actual mismatch, on the very link telling the reader where to report a phishing email.

email.subject: The rate on your savings account is changing
email.bodyText:
The annual percentage yield on your savings account is changing.

From the first of next month the rate becomes 3.65% APY. The new rate applies automatically and there is nothing for you to do.

You can see your balance, the interest earned so far and the full rate history at any time.

Rates are variable and may change again.

To learn more about email security, or to report a message you think is not from us, visit apple.com/security.
